name: HDYHaus Identity Verification
author: Mary Mojisola Job

sections.description:
HDYHaus Identity Verification adds identity verification to the default WordPress registration page. When a provider is enabled, WordPress creates the account only after the provider confirms a successful verification.

HDYHaus Identity Verification is a verification gate, not a membership suite. It does not replace the registration form, add payment processing, restrict content, or create membership levels.

Features

  • Adds identity verification to wp-login.php?action=register.
  • Confirms the result server-side before allowing account creation.
  • Binds each verification to the submitted email, configured widget, and one-time registration attempt.
  • Prevents a completed verification session from being reused for another account.
  • Prevents the same verified identity document from creating another account, even after account deletion.
  • Keeps Sandbox and Live Prembly credentials separate.
  • Supports an optional same-site success redirect with email activation instructions.
  • Lets site owners customize the plain-text consent message, provider policy links, and a website terms/disclaimer page or URL.
  • Stores normalized verification metadata in the WordPress user account.
  • Records successful and failed registration attempts for administrator review, with masked email, outcome filters, and pagination.
  • Lets administrators recover an eligible verified registration by creating and linking the WordPress account and sending a password-setup email, without asking the person to verify again.
  • Lets site owners choose how long unlinked attempts and account-linked records are retained (defaults: 7 and 90 days; configurable from 1 to 365 days).
  • Integrates with WordPress personal data export and erasure tools.
  • Uses a provider adapter architecture, with Prembly as the first provider.

HDYHaus Identity Verification supports identity verification and KYC workflows. Installing it does not by itself make a website compliant with any law or regulatory framework. Site owners remain responsible for their verification policy, lawful basis, privacy notice, retention period, and provider configuration.

External Service: Prembly

This plugin connects to Prembly, an external identity verification service, when Prembly is enabled by a site administrator.

The Prembly browser SDK is loaded from https://js.prembly.com/v1/inline/widget-v3.js on the default WordPress registration page. When a registrant selects Verify Identity, HDYHaus Identity Verification sends their first name, last name, email address, a temporary user reference, the configured Widget Key, and Configuration ID to Prembly. Prembly’s verification interface may collect identity document images, selfies, biometric information, device information, and IP-derived location information according to the checks selected by the site administrator.

When a registrant starts verification, HDYHaus Identity Verification records the username, email, first and last name, consent, environment, start time, and any result reported by the widget in a site-specific WordPress table. The full email address is kept in that table because it is needed to resume registration, create an account, and send account emails; the administrator list masks it. Site owners choose how many days unlinked attempts and account-linked records are retained under Identity Verification > Registration (defaults: 7 and 90 days; configurable from 1 to 365 days). Resume links expire after up to seven days. After the verification interface reports completion, the site’s WordPress server requests the corresponding session from https://backend.prembly.com/api/v1/checker-widget/sdk/sessions/{session_id}/. HDYHaus Identity Verification uses that response to confirm the session status, email address, widget configuration, session ID, and verified document identity. The complete Prembly report remains available in the site owner’s Prembly dashboard. Identity document images, document numbers, selfies, biometric information, raw Prembly responses, and detailed provider reports are not copied into WordPress.

This service is provided by Prembly Inc:

  • Prembly: https://prembly.com/
  • Prembly Data Protection Policy: https://prembly.com/data-protection/

The Data Protection Policy is the default provider policy link. Site administrators can replace it and optionally add a working provider terms or consent URL under Identity Verification > Registration. When WordPress has a website Privacy Policy configured, HDYHaus Identity Verification displays that link separately. Website terms or a disclaimer can also be linked by selecting a published WordPress page or entering a custom URL.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate HDYHaus Identity Verification.
  2. In WordPress, enable Settings > General > Anyone can register.
  3. Open Identity Verification > Settings > Prembly. Copy the Prembly SDK Redirect URL shown there. This is your site’s registration URL, normally https://your-domain.com/wp-login.php?action=register; retain any WordPress subdirectory or development port.
  4. In Prembly, choose Sandbox or Production, then open SDK Setup and create a widget. Sandbox is recommended for testing; you may start with Production if ready for live checks. Create a separate widget for each environment you use.
  5. On Prembly’s Brand Details screen, enter your site name, a short visitor-facing description, and your brand colour. Paste your registration URL into Redirect URL. Leave Webhook URL blank; this plugin has no Prembly webhook receiver.
  6. Configure the document and face checks appropriate for your site, then save the widget. Copy its Configuration ID using Copy Config ID, and its Widget Key from the widget’s Integration panel. Use the widget key beginning wdgt_, not the API Integrations public key.
  7. Return to Identity Verification > Settings > Prembly. Enter both values in the matching Sandbox or Live fields, choose the matching active environment, select Enable Prembly, and save.
  8. Open Identity Verification > Registration to review consent wording and policy links. The optional Success Redirect URL is a same-site page shown after WordPress creates the account. It is separate from Prembly’s Redirect URL, which uses your registration URL.
  9. Add identity verification information to the site’s privacy policy. Suggested text is available under Settings > Privacy.
  10. Test the full registration and password-setup email flow before opening registration to visitors.

For a field-by-field widget walkthrough, see https://github.com/HDYHaus/identity-verification/blob/main/docs/prembly-setup.md.

No Prembly Secret API Key, Organisation ID, or App ID is required for the SDK session confirmation used by this plugin.
sections.faq:
Where can I see verification reports and registration attempts?

The complete identity verification report is available in your Prembly dashboard. In WordPress, open Identity Verification > Registration Attempts to review the local registration record, including its outcome/reason, environment, account-link status, and recovery status. The page supports outcome filters and pagination. WordPress stores registration and consent details needed to resume or resolve the signup; it does not copy the full Prembly report or identity documents.

Can an administrator finish creating an account after successful verification?

Yes, when the attempt is eligible. Open Identity Verification > Registration Attempts, review the attempt, and confirm that no existing WordPress account should be used for that person. The administrator can then create and link the account and send the WordPress password-setup email. Recovery uses the already confirmed verification and does not ask the person to verify again. It is unavailable for failed or expired attempts, attempts already linked to an account, or identities/sessions already associated with an account. Existing username or email conflicts should be resolved using the existing account where appropriate.

Does the user need to repeat verification if account creation did not finish?

After a successful server-confirmed verification where WordPress account creation fails, the plugin records the attempt and emails a secure resume link. The link can restore the registration details without repeating verification and expires after at most seven days. If the link expires, an administrator may still recover the account while the attempt remains eligible and retained.

How long are registration attempts retained?

The site owner controls retention under Identity Verification > Registration. Defaults are 7 days for unlinked attempts and 90 days for account-linked records. Each setting can be configured from 1 to 365 days. Resume links are limited to seven days even when the unlinked retention period is longer. One-way session and identity hashes used to prevent replay may remain after the attempt record is deleted.

Does WordPress store the registrant’s email address?

Yes. The email is stored in the plugin’s WordPress attempt table while the record is retained because the plugin needs it to resume registration, create or link the account, and send the relevant emails. The email is masked in the administrator attempt list. The plugin does not store identity document images, document numbers, selfies, biometric information, raw provider responses, or detailed Prembly reports.

Does HDYHaus Identity Verification replace the WordPress registration form?

No. This plugin integrates with the default WordPress registration screen. It does not currently add verification to WooCommerce, BuddyPress, MemberPress, Ultimate Member, or other custom registration forms.

What happens when Prembly is disabled?

HDYHaus Identity Verification registers no verification hooks or Prembly scripts. Normal WordPress registration continues, and saved Prembly settings are preserved.

Does this plugin send data to a third party?

Yes, when Prembly is enabled and a registrant starts verification. See the External Service: Prembly section for the exact service, data flow, and legal links.

Are secret API keys required or exposed?

No. This integration uses Prembly’s Widget Key and Configuration ID in the browser. The session confirmation endpoint uses the session ID and does not require the Secret API Key, Organisation ID, or App ID.

Does HDYHaus Identity Verification store identity documents or selfies in WordPress?

No. WordPress stores registration details and consent for the retention periods selected by the site owner (defaults: seven days for unlinked attempts and 90 days for linked records). A successfully created account also receives normalized verification metadata and site-specific one-way fingerprints in its user profile. Documents, document numbers, selfies, biometric information, raw Prembly responses, and detailed reports are processed by Prembly and are not copied into WordPress by this plugin.

Can the same verified person create more than one account?

No. HDYHaus Identity Verification derives a site-specific one-way fingerprint from the verified document country, type, and number returned by Prembly. It never stores the document number. The fingerprint is retained after privacy erasure or account deletion so the same identity cannot register again.

Can verification metadata be exported or erased?

Yes. HDYHaus Identity Verification integrates with Tools > Export Personal Data and Tools > Erase Personal Data. Erasure retains one-way session-reference and identity hashes to prevent reuse of a completed verification or identity. Site owners should establish an appropriate retention policy and confirm any separate deletion obligations in Prembly.

Can I change the consent wording and provider links?

Yes. Open Identity Verification > Registration to edit the plain-text consent message and the verification provider’s privacy/data-protection and optional terms/consent URLs. The website’s WordPress Privacy Policy is displayed separately when configured under Settings > Privacy. For your website’s own terms or disclaimer, select a published WordPress page or enter a custom URL. HDYHaus Identity Verification stores the exact accepted wording and a version fingerprint tied to the displayed disclosure for successful registrations.

Does HDYHaus Identity Verification support multisite?

This release is tested for single-site WordPress installations. Multisite and network activation have not been verified and are not currently supported.

Where can I get support?

Report plugin bugs at https://github.com/HDYHaus/identity-verification/issues/. For verification widget configuration, billing, or provider reports, contact Prembly through https://prembly.com/.

Does this make my site KYC compliant?

No plugin can guarantee legal or regulatory compliance. HDYHaus Identity Verification provides an identity-verification gate that can support a site’s KYC workflow. Obtain appropriate legal advice for the site’s countries, audience, and use case.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Clarify registration-attempt recovery, attempt retention, email storage, and where to find provider reports in the plugin description and FAQ.

1.0.0

  • Let site owners configure how long unlinked and account-linked verification attempts are retained, with defaults of 7 and 90 days.
  • Apply retention changes to currently retained records and show the selected periods in the attempts screen and privacy-policy guidance.
  • Keep verification resume links limited to seven days.

0.10.0-beta.6

  • Display attempt timestamps in the WordPress site’s configured timezone and date/time format.

0.10.0-beta.5

  • Show completed and unresolved attempts on the Registration Attempts page.
  • Add successful, failed, and other/pending filters, pagination, and links to created WordPress accounts.

0.10.0-beta.4

  • Quote custom attempt-table identifiers with WordPress’s %i placeholder in prepared queries.
  • Align the prerelease stable tag with the plugin header for development Plugin Check runs.

0.10.0-beta.3

  • Log verification starts and widget-reported failures, cancellations, or errors for admin review.
  • Keep account recovery limited to provider-verified attempts.

0.10.0-beta.2

  • Register the Registration Attempts submenu after its parent admin menu.

0.10.0-beta.1

  • Keep provider-verified registration attempts in a dedicated WordPress table with bounded retention.
  • Email a secure, expiring link so users can finish registration without repeating verification.
  • Add an administrator review screen to create and link accounts for eligible verified attempts.
  • Export and erase registration-attempt personal data through WordPress privacy tools.

0.9.10

  • Include the declared languages directory in the release package.
  • Display the site’s registration URL in Prembly settings for use as the SDK Redirect URL.
  • Explain Brand Details, the blank Webhook URL, and the separate success redirect.
  • Recommend Sandbox for testing while allowing Production-first setup.

0.9.9

  • Link the HDY Haus author credit to the plugin landing page.
  • Use Prembly’s Data Protection Policy and remove the obsolete default Terms link.
  • Correct saved legacy provider policy defaults while retaining custom URLs.
  • Refresh listing screenshots to match the Identity Verification menu label.

0.9.8

  • Rename the plugin to HDYHaus Identity Verification.
  • Use a persistent plugin secret for identity fingerprints independent of WordPress authentication salts.
  • Require a valid registration-form nonce before processing verification fields.
  • Update public repository and support links.

0.9.7

  • Move global registration settings to HDYHaus Identity Verification > Registration.
  • Clarify recommended verification provider privacy and terms links and the website Privacy Policy configuration.
  • Add a published WordPress page selector or custom URL for website terms/disclaimers, included in the consent record fingerprint.

0.9.6

  • Create the settings option directly on its first save so values remain stored after cache flushes and plugin deactivation.

0.9.5

  • Preserve the internal settings-tab marker so fresh installations remain correct when WordPress sanitizes a new option twice.

0.9.4

  • Fix the settings handler so WordPress sanitizes each submission exactly once and persists every field after reload.

0.9.3

  • Fix saving provider activation and Prembly widget settings after a fresh installation.
  • Route settings updates through a nonce-protected HDYHaus Identity Verification admin handler.

0.9.2

  • Prevent one verified identity document from creating multiple WordPress accounts.
  • Retain only a site-specific one-way identity fingerprint after privacy erasure or account deletion.
  • Fail closed when a completed provider response lacks a stable document identity.

0.9.1

  • Add a read-only HDYHaus Identity Verification verification and consent record to WordPress user profile screens for administrators.
  • Show when privacy erasure has removed verification details while retaining replay protection.

0.9.0

  • Require the Prembly session ID, widget configuration, and end-user email to match before registration.
  • Add explicit registrant consent before opening identity verification.
  • Allow site owners to customize consent wording and provider legal links safely.
  • Add WordPress privacy policy guidance and personal data export and erasure support.
  • Correct the Prembly external-service disclosure and current credential requirements.
  • Add provider response and privacy integration tests with repeatable release packaging.

0.1.6

  • Use Prembly’s session-ID-only status lookup and remove unused API key, Organisation ID, and App ID requirements.

0.1.5

  • Apply a same-site success redirect with email activation instructions.

0.1.4

  • Add exclusive provider tabs, provider resolution, and provider-specific advanced settings.

0.1.3

  • Add a top-level HDYHaus Identity Verification admin area, Plugins screen settings link, and separate Sandbox and Live credentials.

0.1.2

  • Use Prembly’s widget-specific key and current V3 browser SDK.

0.1.1

  • Support Prembly V3 SDK session callbacks and server-side session confirmation.

0.1.0

  • Initial development scaffold.
